chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abu Ishaq, from Fayd, from Ash'ath, from al-Hasan (peace be upon him):
Regarding a man who dies while he has a debt, and he had given permission to his slave to trade, and the slave has a debt, he said: 'The master's debt is paid first.'
ai.seo_question: Who gets paid first when both a master and his slave have debts?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the hierarchy of debt settlement when a master dies while his slave is engaged in trade, prioritizing the master's creditors over the slave's. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that the master's estate takes precedence in the distribution of the slave's trading profits or assets, ensuring the master's obligations are fulfilled first. It underscores the legal interdependence between master and slave in commercial transactions during the classical period.
